title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, “Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines” versus Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that comparative shoot length, root length and fresh weight were “taken after 10 days-stress,” but the Figure 3 caption describes the same phenotypic comparison as being conducted under NaCl stresses “kept for 7 days.” These are incompatible exposure durations for the measurements represented by Figure 3 and must be corrected or explicitly distinguished as separate experiments.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 3 caption and associated claims of superior growth/stress tolerance
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The caption reports only “average of three plants ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)” without identifying a statistical test, the comparison for which the P value applies, exact P values, degrees of freedom, multiple-comparison handling, or even whether the three plants are independent biological replicates. A blanket P ≤ 0.05 cannot establish significance for the many line-by-salt-concentration comparisons shown or support statements that one line was “maximum” or “best.”

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, selection and comparison of 7PcINO1, 10PcIMT1 and 6DC1 lines; Abstract conclusion comparing transgene classes
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The central mechanistic comparison is made between independently transformed, selected “best performing” events: “7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line.” No null segregants from the same transformation events, matched independent insertion-event replicates, or complementation/segregation evidence is described for the physiological and metabolite conclusions. Independent transformation events can differ through insertion position, copy structure, somaclonal variation, and selection history. Therefore, the reported difference between a single PcINO1 event and a single PcIMT1 or DC1 event cannot be attributed specifically to inositol versus pinitol pathway manipulation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and concluding interpretation: “inositol itself acts as a stress-ameliorator and/or as a switch”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The reported evidence is correlational: selected lines with higher PcINO1 transcript/protein and inositol also appear more salt tolerant. It does not isolate inositol from the PcINO1 protein, transgene insertion effects, other stress-response changes, or the independently selected genetic backgrounds. No manipulation demonstrating that changing inositol alone changes tolerance is described. The claim that inositol itself is the stress ameliorator or a pathway “switch” is therefore not established by these data.

This section is presented as a “Test of allergenicity” and concludes that the observed sequence-comparison values are “indicative of non-allergenicity.” The only reported procedure is an in-silico similarity search of AllergenOnline Database v15. Such a screen can identify sequence-similarity alerts but cannot demonstrate non-allergenicity of a protein or an edible transgenic crop; it does not assess exposure, protein abundance/stability, digestion, glycosylation, IgE binding, or clinical/allergic responses. The conclusion should be limited to absence of a database sequence-similarity signal under the stated search criterion.
